what: In today's CI, the P8 SIGKILL law's second red on main (run 44428278854, :312 after 31381 ms) was traced to installed Vitest 5.0.5, and a fault plant reproduced it on demand on disposable Linux CI through the new host.yaml p8 suite. Plant A (the worker throttle's trailing timer at ms / 2 with today's `pendingCall ??=` line) went red at the same not-null check after 30805 ms, and its CI_PROGRESS_CUTOFF line showed the journal held only module queued, collected and started for probe.test.ts, with no test start and no beforeEach end. Plant B (the same early timer with Vitest 5.1.0's fix) and the PR head both went green, P8 in 8511 ms and 8510 ms.
cause: Vitest 5.0.5's throttle (dist/chunks/run.BPv-BBRv.js:3804-3820) keeps the already-fired timer in pendingCall, so a trailing call that finds now - last not over 100 ms schedules nothing and the batch with the blocked test is never sent. PR 1624 removed the child's 5-second Vitest deadline, which had flushed that batch, so the failure moved from :356 to :312. Vitest 5.1.0 clears pendingCall before it calls again.
fix: A pnpm patch of vitest@5.0.5 carrying 5.1.0's change, dropped at the bump to 5.1.0 (the lead's ticket). A hand-started p8 suite in host.yaml, since no branch proof run reaches tooling-integration (0602).
test: Plant runs R1 and R2, then 8 green p8 runs in a row at the PR head; main's full runs after the merge.
